On Apr 26, 2017, at 6:12 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

I can't recreate your issue.  I just tried it in the
latest RStan from CRAN 2.15.1 and in the latest CmdStan
and both report the same thing:


SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:


ERROR at line 23

21:    }
22:    model {
23:      real[N] linpred;
             ^
24:      e_a ~ normal(0, 1);

PARSER EXPECTED: <identifier>


with RStan additionally saying:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
 failed to parse Stan model 'ideal' due to the above error.

- Bob

On Apr 26, 2017, at 5:54 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:

I had a Stan program with a bug.  I got the following error in my rstan call:

Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
c++ exception (unknown reason)

It took me forever to figure out the error.  At first I thought it was an rstan thing (i'd just updated R), then I went thru the code line by line and I finally found the problem.  I had this declaration in the model block:

real[N] linpred;

Of course, that was a mistake.  It should've been vector[N] linpred; or real linpred[N];

But that should get caught by the parser, right, and say "error in line 23" or whatever?

For convenience I've attached the offending Stan program.

It was a stupid error on my part, but people do make stupid errors so it would be good to catch these things!

See you
A


<ideal_0.stan>
